title: Reformed grant essence in assent not notitia; notitia not strict science
source_text: LXI. Vicissim vero Doctores Reformati Scholae Romanae Doctoribus concedunt fidei naturam atque essentiam in assensu potius quam in notitia consistere; licet notitia quaedam in fide includatur, aut ad eam praesupponatur. Fatentur quoque notitiam illam, quam includit aut praesupponit fides, non esse scientiam stricte & proprie dictam, id est, cognitionem evidentem rei per causas; nec etiam, si non evidentem, saltem distinctam atque accuratam aliquam notitiam, qua non tantum res, sed etiam modus rei percipiatur.
pass_a_gloss: Conversely the Reformed Doctors concede to the Doctors of the Roman school that the nature and essence of faith consists in assent rather than in knowledge, although some knowledge is included in faith or presupposed for it. They also confess that that knowledge which faith includes or presupposes is not science strictly and properly so called — that is, evident cognition of a thing through causes — nor even, if not evident, at least some distinct and accurate knowledge by which not only the thing but also the mode of the thing is perceived.
pass_b_english: Reformed grant Rome that faith essence is assent rather than notitia, though some knowledge is included or presupposed.
That included knowledge is not strict science (evident cognition through causes) nor even always distinct accurate perception of mode.
